expectations.text: States that a written agreement or reminder is not enforcement
expectations.evidence: "Training (docs, Slack, standups) degrades... developers have to remember to run the formatter—and memory is the weakest part of any system"

expectations.text: Recommends a pre-commit hook to run the formatter automatically
expectations.evidence: "Pre-commit hook (catches it before the branch exists)... Runs formatter + type checker on staged files"

expectations.text: Notes that pre-commit is bypassable with --no-verify and must be backed by a CI check
expectations.evidence: Mentions CI catches what slips through but does not explain the --no-verify bypass mechanism

expectations.text: Recommends a type check as a required CI check
expectations.evidence: Type checker is relegated to pre-commit layer; CI block description focuses on formatting/linting without explicitly requiring type checking

expectations.text: Recommends baselining or ratcheting rather than enforcing across the whole repo at once
Notes that branch protection is what makes a CI check actually required
Recommends the failure message tell the developer how to fix it
Does not primarily recommend rewriting CONTRIBUTING.md, more reminders, or more discipline
expectations.evidence: "They didn't fail because they're careless—they failed because you asked them to remember"; focuses on devices, not discipline
